subject: ent
title: Hearing aids, cochlear implants and the deaf child

steps.tx: **Key point.** Early hearing detection transforms language: congenital deafness missed past infancy delays speech irreversibly during critical brain plasticity windows. Universal newborn screening (otoacoustic emissions then auditory brainstem response) targets diagnosis by three months and intervention by six months (1-3-6 principle in many programmes). Any parental concern about hearing overrides passed screens.
steps.say: Find deaf babies by 3 months and help by 6 months. Parent worry always earns testing even after passed screens.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Causes of childhood deafness include genetic (connexin 26 GJB2 commonest non syndromic), congenital CMV infection, meningitis, prematurity with ototoxic exposure, and syndromes (Usher, Waardenburg, Pendred with goitre). Meningitis can ossify the cochlea within weeks, making implant timing urgent after bacterial meningitis deafness. Speech delay, inattention and television volume are late presentations.
steps.say: Genes and congenital CMV deafen most deaf children. After meningitis, cochlea may bone over fast: implant referral is urgent.

steps.tx: **Hearing aids** amplify sound for mild to severe losses with functioning hair cells, fitted and verified in growing ears with earmoulds and speech therapy support. Bone conduction devices bypass conductive blocks (atresia, chronic drainage) vibrating skull directly. Middle ear implants suit selected adults intolerant of moulds. Aids do not restore normal hearing; classroom acoustics and FM systems matter equally.
steps.say: Aids amplify for working inner ears. Bone vibrators bypass blocked middle ears. Classroom listening support counts as much as devices.

steps.tx: **Cochlear implants** bypass dead hair cells electrically stimulating the spiral ganglion directly, for severe to profound bilateral loss with limited aid benefit. Early implantation (often around or before 12 months in congenital deafness per local criteria) yields best spoken language. Surgery preserves facial nerve and electrodes thread the scala tympani; mapping and years of auditory verbal therapy follow.
steps.say: Implants electrically replace dead hair cells for profound deafness. Earlier in infancy means better spoken language.

right.title: Cochlear implant
points: Severe to profound, poor aid benefit

steps.tx: **Key point.** The deaf child needs whole team care: audiology, ENT, speech language therapy, teacher of the deaf, genetics and ophthalmology (Usher retina), plus family chosen communication (spoken, sign or both). Vaccination (pneumococcal, meningococcal where indicated) protects implant users from meningitis risk. Educational placement and assistive listening decide outcomes as much as device choice.
steps.say: Devices alone do not teach language: team, family communication choice and school support decide deaf children's futures.
